The pipeline, stage by stage

Source: vignettes/pipeline.Rmd
pipeline.Rmd

run_one_source() takes one source from the cohort definition to the harmonized tables. Each stage is also a function you can call yourself, and each writes a log row so a resumed run knows what is already done.

The stages

Stage Writes
cache_raw_parquet A Parquet copy of the raw CSVs for faster repeated reads
import_cohort The selected cohort and window tables, as Parquet or DuckDB
run_db Loads the cohort tables into PostgreSQL
run_raw_mods Builds the raw modifications eICU needs before concepts
build_window_tables The admission, ICU and visit windows in PostgreSQL
build_cohort_annotations The SCI cohort annotations (SCI profile)
build_cohort_info The generic cohort information table
run_comorbidities Charlson and Elixhauser indices
run_iss Injury severity scores
run_concepts The flat, time-series, duration, derived and user concepts
run_external_concepts Registered external SQL modules
run_harmonized_tables The merged flat_tab, ts_tab and dur_tab

The dependency order is fixed; selecting a later stage does not build its prerequisites. A full run uses the profile’s default stages: "scid" adds the cohort annotations, comorbidities and injury severity, while "generic" runs the generic cohort information and leaves the two enrichment stages off unless asked.

On eICU, run_raw_mods builds medication_mod, infusiondrug_mod and admissiondrug_mod, which keep the raw columns and add parsed mod_* columns (drug name, dose or rate, unit, start and stop), and lab_mod and respiratorycharting_mod, which bring FiO2 to percent. Medication orders with a blank drug name are named from their drug code through rendehr_eicu_hicl_drugname_lookup.csv; a file of that name in the project’s config/ directory replaces the shipped one.

Rerunning two stages on the demo reports what they did:

stages <- run_one_source(
  "mimic_iv_demo",
  stages = c("run_concepts", "run_harmonized_tables")
)
stages[, c("stage", "status", "seconds")]
#>                   stage  status    seconds
#> 1          run_concepts success 25.6869235
#> 2 run_harmonized_tables success  0.8692167

A stage that is already complete can be skipped; execution_options(overwrite = TRUE) forces it to run again. run_one_source_test() runs the same stages but also checks their outputs and the pipeline log, which is what the package’s own tests use.

Options without a 47-argument call

The direct arguments still work, and the option constructors group them. An option object carries only the values you set; everything else keeps the receiving stage’s default.

run_one_source(
  "mimic_iv_demo",
  stages = "run_concepts",
  concepts = concept_options(layers = c("flat", "ts")),
  loading = loading_options(threads = 2),
  execution = execution_options(overwrite = TRUE)
)

concept_options(layers = ) selects concept layers in pipeline order: flat, ts, dur, ehr, user, external. Use stages for pipeline stages and layers for concepts; the two are independent. Supplying the same setting both directly and inside a group is an error, even when the values agree.

DuckDB

engine = "duckdb" runs run_db, run_raw_mods, build_cohort_info and run_concepts in DuckDB. The stages that exist only in PostgreSQL (build_cohort_annotations, run_comorbidities, run_iss, run_external_concepts, run_harmonized_tables) are skipped with a message rather than silently ignored.

run_one_source("mimic_iv_demo", engine = "duckdb",
               stages = c("run_db", "build_cohort_info", "run_concepts"))

A DuckDB run is a complete analysis path for the flat, time-series, duration and user layers. To continue it in PostgreSQL, run the PostgreSQL plan from run_db() and reuse the cohort Parquet instead of importing it again.

Several sources

run_sources() calls run_one_source() for each source with the same options:

run_sources(c("mimic_iv_demo", "eicu_demo"))

merge_sources() then pools the per-source schemas into one target schema. The merge grain is an analysis decision: analysis_level = "admission" keeps one row per admission (the first ICU stay), "icu" keeps one row per ICU stay.

merge_sources(c("mimic_iv_demo", "eicu_demo"), target_schema = "rendehr")

Checking the result

The verify_*() functions read a schema and report whether its tables have the expected shape. They are the quickest check after a run, and the same functions the validation levels call.

con <- connect_postgres(ehr_config()$database$db_name, load_credentials())
verified <- c(
  db_load    = verify_db_load(con, "mimic_iv_demo_coh")$ok,
  cohort     = verify_cohort(con, "mimic_iv_demo_coh")$ok,
  concepts   = verify_concepts(con, "mimic_iv_demo_coh_concepts")$ok,
  derived    = verify_handcrafted(con, "mimic_iv_demo_coh_derived")$ok,
  harmonized = verify_harmonized(con, "mimic_iv_demo_coh_harmonized")$ok
)
verified
#>    db_load     cohort   concepts    derived harmonized 
#>       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE       TRUE
ehr_disconnect()

Each call returns a list with ok, the individual checks and their messages; the vector above keeps the verdicts, and a failure names the table and what was missing. The source schemas created by the pipeline are <source>_coh (cohort tables), <source>_coh_concepts (flat, time series and durations), <source>_coh_derived (adapted derived concepts), <source>_coh_harmonized (the three analysis tables) and <source>_coh_ext_external (external modules).
